hook.text: Your eyes send about 10 million bits per second to your brain. Conscious perception uses maybe 50 bits per second.

buildup.text: Massive compression happens between sensory input and awareness. Most information is processed unconsciously.

discovery.text: The retina has 1 million output fibers. But attention selects only a tiny fraction for conscious processing.

twist.text: This isn't a flaw—it's optimal. Consciousness is a bottleneck by design, focusing resources on what matters now.

climax.text: The brain is a massive parallel processor that funnels into a serial conscious stream—a compression pipeline.

punchline.text: Millions of bits in. Fifty bits noticed. The rest is filtered.

quiz.question: How much of the visual input reaches conscious awareness?
options: A tiny fraction—about 50 bits per second
